column2: Ronald dipped the toe in at the Asian grocer the first few times by just visiting the instant noodle aisle. He branched out from there, once the strange lettering and the luminous, colourful packaging became less scary.
Helen always carried a spare pair of goggles in her glove compartment. She'd once been caught in a downpour when her convertible roof had failed to come out - she had vowed never again.
Sally, the self-flagellater with low self-esteem, self-inflicted a self-help book on herself.

It was like half the Westerns Zac had ever seen. Except this time, the tumbleweed was made out of dust and dog hair, and it was blowing across his living room floor with the help of the breeze from an open window. He sighed. It was time to vacuum.
Frustratingly, Shauna's calorie-tracking app didn't cater for the partial food remnants her kids gave her to finish off. As a result, she wasn't getting any closer to her target weight.
Vale Val, the Vape Venus, read the tombstone.

Even as she was expelling the sentence from cold, chaffed lips, about how she was willing to embrace this winter, her thirtieth on record, Taryn was already formulating a trip to Bali.
